key_insight: The paper finds that steering methods work better when they target features that predict what a reasoning model will do next, rather than features that merely detect what it has already said. In short: predicting future behavior is a better intervention target than reading current text.
problem_solved: Test-time steering can control large reasoning models, but existing interventions often reduce output quality because they rely on internal signals tied to already-generated behavior instead of future behavior. This paper addresses how to steer models more effectively without harming generation quality.
method: Analyze internal features used in prior steering methods and show they are mostly detectors of current/past text behavior.
Train activation probes to predict future behavioral outcomes in reasoning models.
Compare these predictive probes against detection-based features as intervention targets for test-time steering.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more reliable way to steer deployed reasoning models while preserving answer quality. It can improve controllability in safety, alignment, and behavior-shaping applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side flow diagram: 'detect current text' vs 'predict future behavior'

paper_title: Predicting Future Behaviors in Reasoning Models Enables Better Steering
paper_authors: Evgenii Kortukov, Piotr Komorowski, Florian Klein, Paula Engl, Gabriele Sarti
